hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image terminates at a wide driveway, forcing pedestrians into a shared space with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side, where the sidewalk meets the dark paved driveway area.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Wide Driveway
hazards.description: The large paved area between the two buildings lacks clear markings or narrowing, creating a wide conflict zone for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, the dark paved area between the two buildings.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Significant cracking and patching in the roadway and near the sidewalk area present potential trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway and the transition to the driveway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Extension and Continuity
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk across the driveway area with a consistent material and elevation to prioritize pedestrian movement.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks to provide designated crossing points for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is cracked and uneven, posing a significant trip hazard for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs, forcing people to cross the street without a designated safe path.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street may hide pedestrians from oncoming traffic, increasing the risk of collisions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway

hazards.name: Wide roadway
hazards.description: The wide, open roadway design lacks traffic calming, which can lead to higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk on left
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a dedicated, separated sidewalk, forcing pedestrians to walk near parked or moving vehicles.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree on the right corner and parked cars on the left may obstruct sight lines between drivers and pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A wide paved driveway on the right crosses the sidewalk, creating a potential conflict zone between pedestrians and turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the driveway meets the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street lighting is visible in the immediate vicinity, which may reduce pedestrian safety and visibility during nighttime hours.

hazards.name: Frequent driveway curb cuts
hazards.description: Multiple vehicle access points for commercial properties on the left create conflict zones where cars cross the pedestrian walkway.

hazards.name: Faded lane markings
hazards.description: The center line is nearly invisible, which can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming traffic if they attempt to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground.

hazards.name: Utility pole
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is located very close to the curb, presenting a fixed-object hazard for vehicles and potentially encroaching on the pedestrian buffer zone.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left curb block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Narrow sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image is very narrow, potentially hindering accessibility.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Driveway
hazards.description: A very wide entrance to a car wash interrupts the sidewalk without any markings or physical cues to indicate pedestrian priority, creating a large conflict zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the sidewalk ends and the car wash asphalt begins.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalk Continuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk terminates at the commercial property line, forcing pedestrians to navigate an undefined space shared with turning vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Mid-ground, between the residential house and the car wash building.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a dedicated pedestrian walkway, forcing people to walk in the roadway or through parking areas.

hazards.name: No Sidewalk Buffer
hazards.description: The existing sidewalk on the right is immediately adjacent to the curb with no buffer from moving traffic or parked cars.

hazards.name: Excessive Driveway Width
hazards.description: The driveway entrance is extremely wide and lacks markings, creating a long, unprotected conflict zone for pedestrians on the main sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the entrance to the commercial area

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk Continuity
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk provided along the access road leading to the commercial buildings, forcing pedestrians to walk in the vehicle travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Center background where a pedestrian is visible in the roadway

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: Significant cracking and wear in the asphalt at the transition point may present a trip hazard.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are placed directly within the sidewalk path on the left, reducing the effective width for pedestrians and those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven surfaces across the roadway create tripping hazards and unpredictable vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Wide Commercial Driveway
hazards.description: A very wide driveway for the car wash and service center increases the distance pedestrians are exposed to vehicle traffic and encourages higher turning speeds.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Hedges
hazards.description: Tall hedges along the right side of the driveway entrance block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles exiting the property.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the driveway entrance.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Large Vehicle
hazards.description: A large fire truck parked on the right side of the road significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars on both sides of the street create potential 'dart-out' hazards where pedestrians might step into the road from between vehicles.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A fire truck parked at the curb completely blocks the view of the roadway for pedestrians and the view of the sidewalk for drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left side of the street

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel/parking lane with no physical separation or furniture zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Multiple wide curb cuts for commercial access points create numerous conflict zones where vehicles cross the pedestrian walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street at the commercial business entrances.

hazards.name: Lack of Protected Crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the roadway without any designated protection or priority.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked vehicles along the curb can block sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: A wide, unmarked vehicle access road to the left of the main building creates a large area where pedestrians must cross vehicle paths without protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, intersecting the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: Despite the presence of an institutional destination (Salvation Army), there is no marked crossing to facilitate safe pedestrian access from the opposite side of the street.

hazards.name: Absence of lane markings
hazards.description: The lack of lane lines can lead to lane drift and higher vehicle speeds due to the perceived width of the road.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalk buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians are separated from moving traffic only by a curb, with no horizontal buffer like a planting strip or parked cars.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: Cracking and patching in the asphalt could present a trip hazard for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Degraded Roadway Surface
hazards.description: Extensive cracking and patching of the asphalt can create uneven surfaces for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: The wide entrance to the parking lot creates a large area where pedestrians on the sidewalk are exposed to turning vehicles without clear priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, where the sidewalk meets the parking lot entrance

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of lane markings on the roadway can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and potentially higher speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Driveway Crossing
hazards.description: A vehicle entrance to a parking lot crosses the sidewalk without clear markings or priority for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the restaurant building

hazards.name: Long Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two lanes of traffic without a median refuge or curb extensions to shorten the distance.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image at the zebra crossing.

hazards.name: Utility pole proximity
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is located at the immediate edge of the curb, potentially creating a fixed-object hazard for vehicles and a minor obstacle for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, at the curb edge.

hazards.name: Shared lane markings (sharrows)
hazards.description: Sharrows indicate cyclists must share the travel lane with motor vehicles, increasing the risk of conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway pavement

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the right side of the image terminates at a wide driveway, forcing pedestrians into a shared space with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side, where the sidewalk meets the dark paved driveway area.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Wide Driveway
hazards.description: The large paved area between the two buildings lacks clear markings or narrowing, creating a wide conflict zone for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, the dark paved area between the two buildings.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Significant cracking and patching in the roadway and near the sidewalk area present potential trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway and the transition to the driveway.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and level the existing sidewalk to provide a continuous, ADA-compliant walking surface.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crossing with high-visibility paint and appropriate signage to designate a safe pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Paint center lines and parking lane boundaries to organize vehicle flow and clarify the road space for all users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a dedicated sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a continuous and safe path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Install Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety after dark.

interventions.title: Driveway Crossing Treatment
interventions.description: Maintain the sidewalk material and grade across the driveway to reinforce pedestrian priority and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Roadway Re-striping
interventions.description: Refresh lane markings to clearly define travel lanes and narrow the perceived roadway width to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Undergrounding Utilities
interventions.description: Remove the utility pole and overhead wires by placing them underground, which eliminates a roadside hazard and improves the visual environment.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Narrowing
interventions.description: Add lane markings to define the travel way and narrow lanes to encourage slower vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk material and level across the driveway to clearly signal to drivers that they are crossing a pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the curb cut to the minimum necessary for vehicle access, shortening the exposure distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Install ladder-style crosswalk markings across the driveway entrance to increase driver awareness of pedestrians.

interventions.title: New Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Install a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, separated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks with ADA-compliant curb ramps at logical crossing points.

interventions.title: Lane Markings and Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Add center line and edge line markings to define travel lanes and consider curb extensions to shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the driveway entrance using curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings across the driveway to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Extension
interventions.description: Construct a new sidewalk along the access road to provide a protected path for pedestrians entering the commercial site.

interventions.title: Midblock Crossing with Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install a marked midblock crosswalk with curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to the buffer zone to ensure a clear, unobstructed walking path on the existing sidewalk.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the driveway to the minimum required for safe vehicle access to slow down turning traffic and shorten the pedestrian crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Sightline Improvement
interventions.description: Remove or trim the tall hedges near the sidewalk to ensure clear sightlines between drivers exiting the driveway and pedestrians on the walkway.

interventions.title: Street Trees or Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a vegetated buffer between the curb and the sidewalk to provide physical separation from traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island or Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) to provide a safe, designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Enhanced Streetscape Buffers
interventions.description: Add consistent street trees or a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway to improve pedestrian comfort and naturally slow vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with high-visibility 'continental' markings and pedestrian crossing signage to provide a designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer / Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone or planting strip between the sidewalk and the curb to increase pedestrian comfort and safety.

interventions.title: Marked Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated crossing point for residents.

interventions.title: Roadway Striping
interventions.description: Add center lines and edge lines to the roadway to better organize traffic flow and encourage slower speeds.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing and Striping
interventions.description: Repair the degraded pavement and add clear center-line markings to better define travel lanes and slow traffic.

interventions.description: Apply paint or different paving materials to the sidewalk where it crosses the driveway to alert drivers to pedestrian presence.
